lines.speaker: e
lines.text: The Army said it had captured a flying disc. A day later, it took that back.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: On a New Mexico ranch, Mac Brazel found tinfoil, rubber and sticks.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: The nearby air base put out a press release: a flying disc, recovered.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: But in Fort Worth, General Roger Ramey showed reporters the debris. A weather balloon, he said.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: For thirty-one years, it went quiet. Then Major Jesse Marcel, who gathered the debris, called it a cover story.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: Later books added alien bodies. So the Air Force reopened its files.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: Its nineteen ninety-four report named Project Mogul, most likely: secret balloon trains built to hear Soviet atomic tests.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: The purple 'symbols' people recalled matched flower-printed tape from a toy maker.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: Mogul was secret. The weather balloon stood in.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: For forty-seven years, that stayed the answer. Nobody explained it.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: There's a space a hundred feet long hidden inside the Great Pyramid. And no one can get in.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: Particles from space found it.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: Cosmic rays rain myoo-ons down through the stone all day, and empty space lets more of them through. Detectors in the Queen's Chamber counted them.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: Above the Grand Gallery, the pyramid's tallest passage, the count jumped. A hidden void, at least thirty metres long.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: Three teams saw it, from three different angles.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: In twenty twenty-three, a smaller hidden corridor got a closer look. A camera thinner than a pencil slid through a gap in the stones, and found it empty, probably unseen for forty-five centuries.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: The big one is different. It sits deep inside millions of blocks. No tunnel reaches it. No camera has been inside.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: Is it a sealed room, or just empty space? Nobody explained it.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: In eighteen ninety-eight, a photographer in Turin developed his plate. The negative showed a face.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: It came from a linen cloth with the faint image of a man. Tradition links it to the burial of Jesus.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: Then science asked: how old is the cloth? In nineteen eighty-eight, one strip was cut from a corner split between Oxford, Zurich and Arizona.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: All three pointed to the Middle Ages, close to when it first appears in records.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: Critics said the corner might be a medieval repair, and statisticians found the lab numbers less consistent than published.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: But a textile restorer found no sign of reweaving, and Arizona's leftover piece looked original.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: A former Nature editor: not substantially wrong, but not definitive. The bigger question was never the date.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: How was the image made? Every study since gives the same answer: Nobody explained it.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: Everyone says the Nazca Lines were drawn to be seen from the sky.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: A machine just found three hundred and three that weren't.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: In Peru's southern desert, people scraped away dark stones to draw a hummingbird, a monkey, a spider, some longer than three football fields.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: Who said they were for the sky? Pilots helped make them famous.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: But in nineteen twenty-seven, Toribio Mejía found them on foot, hiking the foothills.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: For nearly a century, researchers counted about four hundred and thirty figures.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: Then a Japanese team gave aerial photos to an I B M artificial intelligence.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: In six months it led them to three hundred and three new ones. Nearly doubling the count.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: Smaller. Older. Drawn beside walking trails, to be seen by people passing on foot.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: Humans, llamas, and killer whales holding knives.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: So who were the giant ones for? Nobody explained it.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: In nineteen ninety-seven, thousands watched a giant V of lights over Phoenix. Witnesses said it made no sound.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: Later, a row of lights seemed to hang over the city. Hundreds of photos. Hours of video.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: Arizona's governor later called it otherworldly. But look at what the pictures show.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: Amateur astronomer Mitch Stanley aimed his telescope at the V. Five separate planes, flying in formation.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: Air National Guard A-tens on a training run, Operation Snowbird. Steady lights. No blinking.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: And the later lights? Watch the videos to the end. Each light winks out at the same line: the Sierra Estrella mountains.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: They weren't over Phoenix. They were behind the ridge, fifty miles or more away.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: Parachute flares, dropped by Maryland Guard jets over a bombing range. A decade later, one of those pilots confirmed it.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: Believers still repeat one line: Nobody explained it.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: At the centre of Stonehenge lies a six-tonne stone, and for a century everyone agreed where it came from.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: Wales. Every guidebook said: green sandstone, from Welsh hills. It lies pinned under a fallen giant.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: The answer came from two small fragments found at the site. Inside them, tiny crystals, each one a clock of when it formed.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: Wales didn't match. Geologists compared those ages with rocks across Britain. The match was the far northeast of Scotland.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: In twenty twenty-four, geologist Anthony Clarke's team put it in Nature: the stone travelled at least seven hundred and fifty kilometres.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: Over land, that means mountains, with six tonnes on board. So the team thinks it went by sea.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: Who built that boat, the crystals can't say. The old guidebooks had one line for it: Nobody explained it.
